legend: This metastasis to the lymph node is occurring in a family with a known SDHB mutation.

Primary paraganglioma of the liver can occur and is not always metastatic, albeit rare in this location. This paraganglioma was however favoured to be metastatic as the individual had widespread metastatic paraganglioma.

This paraganglioma is very cellular and associated with necrosis. Although no single histological finding reliably predicts metastases, adverse findings include necrosis, high cellularity, diffuse growth, large tumour size, resectability, as well as the molecular status of the tumour. This tumour was associated with SDHB mutation and metastatic disease.

This paraganglioma shows characteristic Zellballen nesting that is often seen in paragangliomas. The nests are separated by a delicate fibrovascular network. In this case, the nests are quite tight and round, which can be seen in succinate dehydrogenase–related tumours. This tumour also shows cytoplasmic eosinophilia, vacuoles, and clearing, which may also be seen in succinate dehydrogenase–related tumours. This example is from an individual with germline SDHB mutation.
This paraganglioma shows nuclear atypia and nuclear pleomorphism. Although the nuclei in paragangliomas are usually round to oval, they can be pleomorphic or hyperchromatic.
